3,962 likes, 98 comments - financebyanmoll on February 29, 2024: "TEDx was my dream!🥹🥹

It would be a LIE, if I say so.

Never have I ever had envisioned giving a TEDx talk for fraction of a second. I’m a firm believer in trusting the PROCESS.🍀✅

Rest everything are dividend of your efforts.

In the past 4 years, my journey has had its highs and lows, each one of which I cherish. 

Be it founding a startup in my 2nd year of college and failing at it or my interest in finance paying off while creating content, each step of the way I’ve learnt something new which sticks with me forever. 

Because of that whole journey riddled with mistakes and amends, I wasn’t ecstatic when I delivered my first TEDx speech, it felt natural to speak about my journey and what one could learn or avoid from it. 

I’m a big fan of ‘being honest with yourself’. In today’s world, there are many who follow the ‘fake it until you make it’ philosophy but one should be honest with himself/herself. 🤞

Let your actions speak for you. You can fake or you can lie to anyone about life, work, or business but you can’t lie to yourself. 

So staying honest and true to oneself and taking productive steps, one day at a time, you’ll be damn close to achieving anything in life.

But one thing for sure, the Tedx happened because of YOU guys!!! I Love you, and thank you for being a part of this community:)))🌟🍀🫰

#tedx #firsttedx #tedxtalks".

20K likes, 654 comments - financebyanmoll on October 28, 2024: "Every Middle-Class Boy’s Dream! 🥹🚙🥹

This post isn’t only my story; but millions of boys & girls like me who’ll be buying their First Family Car very soon or aspire to gift a car to their parents.

Growing up, the first vehicle my father had was a second-hand red Chetak Scooter, then he bought a second-hand Splendor 6-7 years ago, which he still uses.

So, this car isn’t just our First Family Car ever but also our first new vehicle purchase.

After graduating from college, you wish to buy a car for your parents and yourself, and I dreamed that too.

But the dream took pace when 7 months ago, I decided that I’ll buy a car this Diwali. I passionately believe in Manifestation, because dreams happen first in the mind and then in reality.

And the funniest part, saving for the car wasn’t the toughest job but convincing parents to let me buy a car was extremely tough.

Papa was like, “Hum kyaa karenge gaadi ka, itni mehngi car kyun hi leni?”

But finally, it happened today. We have our first car.

Now, I know, we all see so much content floating around about the ‘Rent vs Buy a House’ argument or ‘buying a new car vs old car,’ but over the years, I’ve realized now that all of this is bullshit.

You don’t buy a car or home, looking at Excel numbers. Obviously, you only buy these things when you can afford them or the EMIs are within your limits, but it’s an emotional decision and should be treated that way. That’s my take!

But coming to that middle-class dream, guys, work hard for it, manifest, and I hope all of you’ll achieve it sooner or later.

And thank you so much, everyone who has supported us throughout the years.

This is the real success. To make your parents happy. To let them enjoy things that they sacrificed for us growing up!!!

Anmol 🤌🏻".

3,246 likes, 87 comments - financebyanmoll on October 10, 2026: "“This market will never recover!”❌

“FIIs are continuously selling. Who’s going to buy Indian equities?”🇮🇳

“The Indian rupee is heading towards ₹100 against the dollar!”💰

“The Indian economy is collapsing. There’s no hope left!”😭

And a few years later?👀🕐

“I wish I had bought more!”✅

“Why did I panic and sell?”😅

“I missed such a golden opportunity!”🤝

Funny how every market crash looks like a disaster in the present and an opportunity in hindsight.🧠

2000, 2008, 2020. Different crises, different narratives, SAME human psychology.

Markets have never moved in straight lines. Bull runs, corrections, consolidations, recoveries. It’s a cycle, not the end of the world.

The real wealth creators understand this.

Everyone wants to buy at the bottom. Nobody wants to live through the fear that creates it.

And a few years from now, people might look back at this very phase and say the exact same thing:

“I wish I had bought more.”

Don’t borrow the crowd’s fear. Opportunities rarely feel like opportunities when you’re living through them.

#financebyanmoll".

318 likes, 27 comments - financebyanmoll on October 8, 2026: "People are frustrated and exhausted by this prolonged sideways phase in Nifty, which has lasted for almost two and a half years.

But we need to understand that these phases are a very normal part of market cycles. After a strong bull run, markets often go through consolidation, corrections, and periods of underperformance.

Eventually, valuations become attractive, pessimism fades, and the next bull run begins. This cycle has repeated itself throughout market history.

So don’t be surprised or behave as if something extraordinary is happening. This isn’t the first time, and it certainly won’t be the last.".

803 likes, 30 comments - financebyanmoll on October 7, 2026: "When big industrial groups start owning critical infrastructure like airports, profit will eventually take priority over passenger comfort.

Redeveloping Mumbai T1 is understandable. But forcing a chunk of international traffic away from T2 also raises another question: is this partly a strategic move to push traffic towards the new Navi Mumbai Airport?

Maybe it’s operational necessity. Maybe it also helps accelerate adoption of a new airport within the same ecosystem.

That’s the problem with crony capitalism , when ownership becomes concentrated, it gets harder to tell where public convenience ends and corporate interest begins. 💰✈️".

1,049 likes, 31 comments - financebyanmoll on October 2, 2026: "We humans are always driven by narratives and sentiments.

Right now, market sentiment is weak. There’s fear, negativity and pessimism everywhere.

But if you think exactly like everyone else, you might miss the opportunities being created right now.

I’m not saying everything looks good or that the market will start rallying from here.

But when pessimism becomes extreme, that’s usually when you should start looking at the other side and searching for opportunities.

As Warren Buffett said, “Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.”

So don’t get completely swayed by the narrative that markets are bearish and everything is bad.

Always look at the other side too.".

1,162 likes, 32 comments - financebyanmoll on September 15, 2026: "Today’s fall was brutal. 🔴

After a relatively calm market since May, today was probably the first time in months that we saw this kind of extreme volatility return, especially in the broader markets.

Midcaps & Smallcaps fell over 2%, Microcaps over 3%, and Defence corrected nearly 5%.

Crude oil is still around $107, while US bond yields remain elevated, both are adding pressure to global markets.

And then we have the Bank of Japan meeting on 18th September. With the possibility of a rate hike, Yen Carry Trade unwinding could create further volatility in emerging markets.

Maybe the market has already started discounting some of that risk through today’s fall.

But there’s a positive side too. 👀

RSI is reaching oversold levels, and on smaller timeframes, we can see signs of divergence as well.

Nifty Midcap 150 has reached an important support zone and is potentially forming a double bottom. Nifty too is approaching similar double-bottom levels, with 23,000 being an important psychological zone.

And here’s another interesting point:

This is now the 6th consecutive week where Nifty is in the red. After such a prolonged stretch of negative weekly returns, the possibility of a rebound naturally starts increasing.

So if the market manages to absorb the upcoming BOJ-related volatility, a rebound from these levels is very much possible. 📈

For now, no predictions: just react to what the market gives us, respect your stop-losses, and follow your system. ❤️".

In recent years, BSE has clearly grown faster across multiple metrics, which means NSE will need to step up to maintain its dominance.

But NSE still has a major advantage in terms of scale, trading volumes and a more diversified revenue mix.

So while BSE has been gaining ground, NSE still has the strength to make a strong comeback.

And ultimately, both can continue to grow and coexist in India’s stock exchange duopoly.

#nseipo".
